subject: SIG: Clarify data extraction, retraining & prompt-log retention
messages:
From: Priyanka Shah <priyanka.shah@novamed.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: security@novamed.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 07:08:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up — use of customer content for model retraining and log retention

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking SIG requests — a few follow-ups from our security team as we review Redwood's SIG answers. We want to confirm three things specifically before we move forward in procurement:

1) Does Redwood ever extract or copy customer prompt/content and use it to further train Redwood models or any public models without explicit, documented opt-in from the customer? If so, what is the exact process and legal basis?

2) How long are generation prompts, responses, and system/meta headers retained in Hosted API production logs? Are there different retention windows for logs used only for debugging vs. logs retained for analytics?

3) Are there any scenarios where prompt/response logs (or backups) are stored outside the customer's specified region or retained longer for forensics/debugging? If yes, what controls exist (e.g., encryption, access logs, RBAC)?

If you can point us to any evidence artifacts (SOC2 report, redacted sample logs, architecture diagram showing KV cache scope), that would be ideal. We're on a tight cycle and would appreciate a response this week.

Thanks — Priyanka
Priyanka Shah
Sr. InfoSec Manager, NovaMed

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Shah <priyanka.shah@novamed.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — use of customer content for model retraining and log retention

Hi Priyanka — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; attaching a short evidence packet and the updated SIG answer PDF. Neha (security) and Rishi (privacy) are CC'd for any deeper controls or contract questions.

Summary (short):
- Training/onboarding: Redwood does NOT use customer content from Hosted API for model training by default. Any use of customer-provided content for model improvement requires an explicit contractual opt-in (Data Use Agreement) and a cross-functional approval process (legal + product + security).

- Prompt/log retention (Hosted): default retention for generation request logs (prompts + responses + system metadata) is 14 days for debugging and SRE/ops analytics. After 14 days logs are rotated and retained in aggregated metrics only. Customers can opt into longer retention windows via account settings or enterprise contract; in that case retention windows are explicitly documented in the contract.

- KV cache and ephemeral state: KV cache used by the runtime is ephemeral and scoped to the inference session; we do not persist KV cache contents to long-term logs by default.

- Backups & forensics: backups that contain transient logs are kept only in the same region as the customer's workload and are encrypted with customer or Redwood-managed KMS (depending on the plan). Access to backups is logged and strictly limited to on-call SRE with approved escalation; any access generates an auditable event in our audit log.

- Private / VPC deployments: customers who run Redwood Private retain full control over retention and telemetry; Redwood's default training policy does not apply to customer-controlled private deployments unless explicitly agreed.

Attachments I included: redwood_sig_answers_v2.pdf (answers table + QA), SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (attestation), kv_cache_architecture.png (diagram showing ephemeral flow). Links: shared Drive folder with sample redacted logs and our evidence checklist.

If you need a redacted sample prompt log with PII masked, tell us how many examples you want and a redaction spec and we will produce a small set under NDA.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions Security 
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — quick clarifications

Marissa — thanks for the quick summary and the attachments. A couple of short clarifications from our engineering/security reviewers:

1) The 14-day default: does that window apply to persisted disk logs only, or also to any intermediate streaming buffers/temporary storage used during inference?

2) For customers on Hosted API who opt into extended retention via an account flag, where is the configuration stored and who can change it (user vs. RedWill ops)?

3) For backup copies used for forensic recovery: are there any automated processes that would copy logs to a different region for DR and, if so, how long are those copies retained?

Appreciate the help — these are gating items for our legal team.

— Priyanka

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Shah <priyanka.shah@novamed.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — quick clarifications

Hi Priyanka — quick clarifications below:

1) 14-day window: applies to persisted logs in our production logging pipeline (disk-backed stores and object storage). Streaming buffers used during a single inference call are memory-resident and discarded immediately after the request; those are not included in retention counts.

2) Extended retention flag: for Hosted API this is an account-level configuration stored in our control plane. Customers with admin privileges on the account can request the change; for standard accounts changes are self-serve via the Console (with an audit trail). For enterprise accounts the flag is set by Redwood only after contract updates; those changes are visible in the Console and in the account's audit log.

3) Multi-region DR copies: we do not routinely replicate prompt/response logs across regions for Hosted API. Disaster recovery for customer workloads is implemented at the model-serving and infrastructure layer, not by copying raw prompt/response logs to other regions. In narrow DR scenarios (region outage with active incident response), ephemeral copies may be created in a DR region for triage; those are short-lived, encrypted, and logged, and we enforce a TTL (24–72 hours) for those emergency artifacts unless a customer authorizes longer retention.

If you'd like, Neha can run through our audit-log sample (who accessed what and when) and Rishi can share contract language we use for explicit training opt-ins. Happy to set a 30-min call this week to walk the NovaMed team through the artifact pack.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Solutions Security
Redwood Inference
